---
title: Manage Resource Lifecycle
description: Activate, archive, copy, and edit resources in place, including how to change an active one.
---

# Manage Resource Lifecycle

Resources move through three states:

- **Mutable**: properties can be edited and saved.
- **Active**: resource is finalized for use. Edits create a copy unless you
  opt in to editing in place.
- **Archived**: resource is retained for history and cannot be edited.

## Activate a resource

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id) as builder:
    with builder:
        builder.finalize()
```

Activation and preceding edits commit when builder exits normally.

### Finalize children in bulk

By default, `finalize()` uses `recursive_depth=0`, targeting only the resource
itself. To finalize the resource and its direct children in one lifecycle
transaction:

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id) as builder:
    builder.finalize(recursive_depth=1)
```

Use `recursive_depth` to control how far below the resource to traverse. The
resource itself is at depth 0; direct children are at depth 1, and grandchildren
at depth 2. Finite depths must be non-negative integers; `None` means all
descendants.

```python
# Include children and grandchildren.
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id) as builder:
    builder.finalize(recursive_depth=2)

# Include all descendants, regardless of depth.
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id) as builder:
    builder.finalize(recursive_depth=None)
```

Traversal includes persisted descendants even if you have not opened child
builders, as well as children saved by the enclosing builder. Only mutable
resources transition to active. Active resources retain their revisions and
timestamps, but traversal continues through them. Archived resources and
their entire subtrees are skipped. Finalizing an archived resource is a no-op.

The lifecycle changes use bulk SQL updates in one transaction, rather than
a transaction and graph refresh for every child. Pending draft edits are
saved before finalization and may use separate transactions. The finalization
still checks the parent revision; a stale revision fails without partially
finalizing the subtree.

Repeated finalization requests within one builder context combine their scopes:
a parent-only or shallower request does not cancel an earlier deeper request.
Pending child archive requests are applied before recursive finalization, so
those archived branches are skipped.

## Archive a resource

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id) as builder:
    builder.archive()
```

Archiving retains resource and provenance while removing it from mutable
lifecycle.

## Edit frozen resources with copy-on-write

By default, editing an active resource through a builder saves your changes
to a new mutable copy and leaves the source untouched. To make the copy
explicitly:

```python
from recap import ResourceCopyOptions

copied = namespace.copy_resource(
    source_resource_id=plate.id,
    options=ResourceCopyOptions(name="Sample Plate 001 Revision"),
)

with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=copied.id) as builder:
    builder.resource.properties["dimensions"].values["rows"] = 16
    builder.finalize()
```

Copy-on-write preserves frozen source and records lineage from copy to source.

## Edit an active resource in place

When an active resource holds a mistake, or holds state that legitimately
changes over time, pass `in_place=True` to change it directly. Given an active
resource `sample`:

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=sample.id, in_place=True) as builder:
    builder.resource.properties["details"].values["concentration"] = 2.5
```

The resource keeps its ID and `ACTIVE` status, and its revision increments.
This also works for a child of an active resource. In-place editing changes
names and values and can add child resources. Child additions and owner content
changes are submitted atomically. Child removal is not supported.

Finalized process runs also default to copy-on-write: edits through
`build_process_run` save to a new mutable copy unless you pass
`in_place=True`. Given a finalized process run `run`, edit it in place:

```python
with namespace.build_process_run(process_run_id=run.id, in_place=True) as run_builder:
    params = run_builder.get_params("Collect")
    params.inputs.values.exposure.value = 0.2
    run_builder.set_params(params)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## In-place edits rewrite history

Process runs that already reference an edited resource see the new values.
The revision number is the only record of the change. Use copy-on-write when
you need to preserve what a run originally used.
:::

Archived resources and runs cannot be edited, even with `in_place=True`.
